about: M63.1: durable wakes. Each scenario starts from an empty agent_wakes and runs its steps in order, each at its own instant. admit offers matches as the renderer sends them (an event wake's key is 64 lowercase hex, its trigger 16, its agent process: and a handle of [a-z0-9-], its cause kind event) and answers how many were admitted, how many were already live, and each refusal in offer order. claim, finish and cancel name a wake by its key, meaning the latest wake admitted with it; claim answers started (the cause the run records and the subjects it took with it), deferred with its reasons, gone, or an error that writes nothing. finish ends the claimed run with a run outcome. pause pauses or resumes an agent on the fleet. expire cancels pending wakes past ttl_days. pending lists the pending wakes inside ttl_days, oldest first. rows lists every wake in admission order. Replayed by src-tauri/src/runtime/wakes.rs and src/lib/mockIpc.test.ts. M63.2 attribution_cases seed recorded writes and root-first run facts, then offer exact versions; rows assert recorded authors and parentage. Repeat checks skipped-cycle deduplication. Shared replay reads each write through writer_of, not a supplied verdict. M63.3b release names agent, subject and a validated assigned key prefix; it cancels pending assignments only and is idempotent.

scenarios.why: a live key is ignored while pending or started, and admitted again once finished
a paused agent and each malformed offer are refused one by one, in offer order
a claim takes the pending event wakes of its own trigger and agent, and no others
a claim that names its own wake again, or another agent's wake, is refused and writes nothing
one agent runs one wake at a time; the next waits a minute, then starts
pausing an agent cancels its pending wakes, which can no longer be claimed; resuming cancels nothing
cancel names its why and touches pending wakes only; an unknown why writes nothing
a wake waits at most seven days: the pending read leaves it out, a claim or the sweep expires it
assignment removal releases only its pending agent page and field, then a re-add is new work
an assigned wake admits once and runs alone; removal cannot cancel a started assignment
